text:
Jordan: Heads-up — planning a short safety sprint to flip the cache+batch feature flag for the main serving pool. Intend to run a canary next Wed 10:00 PDT. Quick Qs: canary size, telemetry we need, and rollback plan?

Maya: +1. Recommend 2% of traffic for canary (mix of short and long sequences). Will that work for the seq-length distribution? :thinking_face:

Alex: 2% sounds fine. Please include at least one heavy seq workload (>=2048) in the canary to exercise KV cache behavior.

Pat: For telemetry: latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), token throughput, error rate, and GPU memory growth over time. Also watch model output quality diffs on our eval prompt set (run eval at t0, t+15m, t+60m).

Jordan: Got it — canary will include a short (<=256) and a heavy (>=2048) traffic slice. Maya, can you add the eval job? Alex/Pat can you confirm dashboard widgets?

Maya: I’ll wire up an autoscheduled eval job that posts results to the canary channel and to the console. Will push a short script:```bash
# run evals for canary
python infra/evals/run_eval.py --subset canary --out canary_eval.json
```

Alex: I’ll add latency + mem dashboards. Quick note: add KV cache hit-rate and KV cache sizes per shard. Those are the key signals for cache regressions.

Lee: From infra side, ensure the rollout policy has an automatic rollback trigger: if p99 latency increases >100ms or error rate >0.5% for 5m, rollback. Also add a manual rollback playbook link in the rollout window.

Jordan: Can you drop the rollback playbook here, Lee?

Lee: Paste of the minimal rollback commands:```bash
# rollback cache-batch FF to OFF for pool-prod
./tools/ff-toggle --env prod --flag cache_batch --state off --actor ops@redwood.com
# or via console: Settings > Feature Flags > cache_batch > toggle OFF
```

Lee: Also: to scale back quickly we have a cheaper path — route traffic to smaller instances without cache using routing policy: tag no-cache-variant. That avoids full capacity pressure.

Pat: One more guardrail: cap canary to 10QPS per model to avoid bursty long-context jobs from pounding KV stores.

Jordan: Good call. I'll update the canary config: 2% traffic, 10QPS per model cap, mix of seq lengths.

Maya: Small ops note: when enabling batching with caching, start with conservative batching windows: 10ms/8 tokens. We can tune after 30m if p95 improves.

Alex: Performance validation steps I'm tracking:
- baseline snapshot (latency, throughput, mem)
- enable canary on pool-A
- run canary traffic for 30m with eval jobs at 0/15/30
- compare diff and sanity-check outputs (BLEU / perplexity / model-specific checks)

Jordan: Who's owner for the canary window next Wed 10:00? I'll volunteer to coordinate and run rollback if needed but need an oncall to watch infra metrics. @Pat? @Lee?

Pat: I can be oncall for that window. Will also put a tiny alert: p99 +100ms OR errors >0.5% triggering pager.

Lee: I'll be watching infra dashboards and have the rollback commands ready. Will also validate the routing policy is applied correctly.

sre-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window for canary must be registered in incidents channel at least 24h prior.

Jordan: Thanks — will post to #incidents today. One last ask: code review ping — the FF config change is in CL 3456. @Alex can you give a quick review on the rollout gating logic?

Alex: On it. Skimming CL now. If we need to adjust thresholds I’ll comment inline. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Deploy check OK for canary config (no conflicts).

Jordan: Awesome. Final checklist before I post to incidents: canary size 2%, seq mix short+heavy, 10QPS cap per model, eval jobs @0/15/30, rollback commands + auto-rollback triggers, dashboards + KV signals, oncall: Pat, infra watcher: Lee. Anything missing?

Maya: Add note to not enable on the EU pool during business hours — cross-region perf differences.

Jordan: Good catch — will limit canary to us-west pool only.

Pat: Also: ensure logs include FF decision ID in request metadata so we can group traces by flagged vs non-flagged.

Jordan: Will add that to the CL. Thanks everyone — I’ll post a concise incident/maintenance note and send calendar invite for Wed 10:00 PDT. :thumbsup:
